topic: B2B SEO, Content Strategy, and AI Search Visibility
headline: Why Building Trust Through Real People Stands The Test Of Time In SEO & AI Search via @sejournal, @lilyraynyc
keyNotes: Many quick ways to get websites noticed on search engines, like using automated tools or shortcuts, often fail in the long run, even if they seem to work for a short time. The article mentions that sites using these methods often end up worse off, sometimes spending years fixing problems.

Google, the company behind the most popular search engine, has been giving the same advice for over 20 years: create content for real people, not just to trick their search engine. As far back as 2003, they warned against "cookie cutter" approaches that lack original content.

Even though new AI tools can create a lot of content very cheaply, Google has been against automatically generated content without human review for a long time. As early as 2010, a Google expert warned that using automated translation without a human checking it first could violate their guidelines.

The most reliable way to succeed online, even with new technologies like AI, is to focus on real people and their expertise in your marketing efforts. This means having identifiable experts stand behind the content you create, rather than just producing generic, machine-made text.
question: The article highlights that creating a lot of content just for search engines, without real people reviewing or standing behind it, eventually causes problems. In your own work or industry, where might the temptation to prioritize speed or quantity over genuine human expertise lead to long-term issues, and how could you ensure human quality remains central?
